notes.sol: The original Figshare v1 script still blocks the primary task-score claims C1, C2 and C5 through missing GMHWG, so the paper remains technical failure. The independent SUS branch computes C3/C4 without reconstructing that object. Sol freshly downloaded v1, confirmed the existing ce9f3a01... source pin and 86898d52... archive pin, checked the SUS data against the pinned archive extraction, and executed 16 unchanged dependency-complete SUS expressions successfully. The broader statement-by-statement check agrees; it is not a successful whole-script run. The audit/v1.1 check used SHA-256 5527a2a9..., a substantively different script (including changed figure logic), not Figshare v1 or a simple newline variant. Therefore the claims pin is retained, and the audit log alone is not the scoring provenance. Both pilot certificates corroborate the SUS values; Sol's pilot additionally checked W under R 4.2.2.
notes.claude: v1.1: C3 and C4 are computable from shipped code (C3 match, C4 discrepant P2); C1, C2 and C5 remain blocked, so the paper stays technical failure. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: CODECHECK/AGILE report: only figures and Table 5 were assessed, and the reviewer obtained updated code via communication with the authors to fix 'missing columns in GMHWG CSV' / 'Sum_GM_Group2'. Static check of the pinned v1 script: it parses in R (419 expressions), but GMHWG is never assigned and is first used at line 771. SUS_ScoresGroup2 is used at line 777 before its assignment at line 1079. Figshare v2 (2023-02-28, adds README) also never creates GMHWG, so the fix is not on Figshare in either version. C3/C4 code does not depend on GMHWG and could be run interactively line by line, but the sourced script dies first and no one reported values. That is why I used P0 not_checkable rather than leaving them unassessed. Minor claim-list nit: the paper labels the between-group tests 'Wilcoxon signed-rank test', but the code runs unpaired (rank-sum) tests. The claim text ('rank-sum W') is correct.
